column1: # ProteinGym substitution-fitness re-run for what the EXP-R2-240 non-text gap
# campaign left open: one score cell to re-run after a code fix, plus the
# MODEL−LOOKUP analysis two of that campaign's scored cells still owe.
# The campaign on freeze 20260916101650_39982a07f55e ran
# 2026-09-16T17:21:47Z–17:40:18Z and ended INCOMPLETE: exited-ok=4,
# exited-nonzero=2, `# NO-RECORD 0`. This manifest carries exactly what that
# outcome leaves to run, and nothing else.
# pgym_instructprotein: RE-RUN. It failed with `ValueError: instructprotein:
# tokenizer, config, input and output vocabulary sizes disagree: 50287, 50304,
# 50304, 50304`. That was a real defect: the guard conflated the model's own
# self-consistency with `len(tokenizer) <= input_vocab`, two invariants a
# padded embedding satisfies only one of. Commit 42f84ab splits the guard into
# those two invariants, makes the renderer assert that no emitted id reaches
# `len(tokenizer)`, and records the padded tail as a measured fact. The cell's
# definition is unchanged by that fix, so the arguments below are the failed
# cell's own, kept byte-identical to
# campaign_proteingym_nontxt_gap.tsv's row and to its `expect` basename.
# pgym_proteinglm-7b-clm: NOT re-run HERE, and that earlier decision has since
# been SUPERSEDED. It failed with `ValueError: ProteinGLM budget prefix+L
# exceeds seq_length 1024`, and this manifest first recorded it as an explicit
# refusal under the fail-fast rule -- no truncation, subset or windowing.
# That was wrong in one respect: the protocol already declares the rule the cell
# should follow (docs/PROTEINGYM_EXTENSION_PROTOCOL.md: an assay is excluded
# when the maximum rendered length exceeds that checkpoint's context, and
# truncation is refused), so the failure was in the length probe, which lost the
# whole arm rather than the 16 assays its 1024 window excludes. Commit 86bad4e
# makes that probe total without moving any scoring-path refusal, and commit
# 4e9f578 dispatched it. The cell is therefore not part of this manifest, but it
# is no longer a refusal: the superseding definition is
# scripts/transfer/campaign_proteingym_proteinglm_rerun.tsv, and its outcome is
# the one to read.
# pgym_zymctrl: NOT re-run. It exited 0 and scored 0 of 217 assays
# (`assays: []`, `skipped[217]`, every skip the wild type's absence from the
# EC-labelled evaluation corpus). That is a corpus-driven total refusal and a
# measurement outcome, not a defect, so it owes no cell and prompts no change.
# The 13 pure-text text-AA columns are out of scope by user decision. None of
# them is in this manifest.
# pgym_progen2-small (201 assays, 16 skipped) and pgym_progen2-base (213
# assays, 4 skipped) both exited 0 under the previous freeze and no analyse
# was ever run against either payload, so neither has a MODEL−LOOKUP. That
# analysis is owed and is the second cell here.
# Which analyse, and the evidence for it — it is stage 20's OWN `analyse`, not
# the native helper and not the scale ladder:
#   * `native_dms_extension.py` cannot serve these arms. `_arm_family` returns
#     only "galactica" or "rita" and raises `KeyError` for `progen2-small`, so
#     the previous campaign's CPU row could name `--probe rita-xl=` and nothing
#     else. The supplement protocol states the same boundary ("不经
#     native_dms_extension.py，那个 helper 的家族表只有 Galactica/RITA").
#   * `42_scale_capability.py`, which produced the
#     progen2-medium/large/xlarge MODEL−LOOKUP numbers, is fixed at those exact
#     three rungs (`SCALE_RUNGS`) and requires a stage-29 directory plus a full
#     stage-41 report, so it cannot take small or base at all.
#   * the EXP-R2-226 lineage arms are the closest precedent for a stage-20
#     panel/corpus arm: their MODEL−LOOKUP lives in
#     results/transfer/r226_lineage/retrieval_bound/retrieval_bound.json,
#     written by this stage's own `analyse` over a directory holding
#     `model_<arm>.json` beside `lookup.json`, `profiles.json` and
#     `wildtypes.json`. No campaign manifest has ever carried a stage-20
#     `analyse` cell; campaign_r226_lineage.tsv and
#     campaign_r228_context_homologue.tsv both record that this stage's analyse
#     "runs on the workstation over the pulled artefacts". Doing it in-pod is
#     what this cell adds, and `analyse` loads no model, so a cpu row is the
#     right resource.
# `analyse` reads all five of its inputs from its own `--out` and has no path
# flags, so they are staged into the cell directory before dispatch — the same
# practice the EXP-R2-224 and EXP-R2-225 dispatches record for `wildtypes.json`
# and `cohort.json`. The five, with their frozen digests:
#   wildtypes.json           45503 B  e080a37758e29c664d71e2a080f990f0bc0e8efdffbae7678b4a8b6271045faa
#   lookup.json             335133 B  the frozen LOOKUP channel, 217 assays / 174 families
#   profiles.json            73862 B  the frozen UniRef50 profiles, 187 wild types
#   model_progen2-small.json 53958 B  from the previous run's pgym_progen2-small cell
#   model_progen2-base.json  54113 B  from the previous run's pgym_progen2-base cell
# The two payloads are copied in-pod from
# results/external_baseline/20260916101650_39982a07f55e/<cell>/ and verified
# against the SHA-256 sidecars the queue wrote beside them. `wildtypes.json`,
# `lookup.json` and `profiles.json` are the frozen stage-20 input set; the
# first two are already on GPFS, `profiles.json` is staged from the
# repository's own copy.
# Both arms are analysed in ONE invocation and ONE artefact. That is the
# project's own convention for a group analysis (EXP-R2-225's Galactica group
# analyse is one cell over four rungs) and it is also the smallest complete
# solution: the shared 217-assay control block is computed once, from one
# `lookup.json` and one seed, so the two MODEL−LOOKUP numbers come out of one
# frozen invocation rather than two that must agree with each other.
# Assay coverage is NOT intersected. `stage_analyse` loops per arm over that
# arm's own `model["assays"]` and looks each one up in the frozen catalogue,
# raising if LOOKUP does not carry it or if the mutant digest differs; it
# never forms a common assay set across arms. So the 201-assay arm and the
# 213-assay arm are each read on their own support, and each payload's
# `skipped` list is carried into its own `assays_skipped`. The per-arm
# `mean_spearman.lookup` therefore differ, which is the visible signature of
# per-arm support rather than a silently narrowed one. The one whole-benchmark
# statement in the file, `blosum62_reproduces_frozen`, is withheld unless the
# support is all 217 assays, which neither arm reaches.
# Two cells. The score cell keeps the failed cell's own frozen definition on
# gpu 0; the analyse cell is cpu, and its inputs as described above. `--seed
# 20260807` and `--bootstrap 2000` are each stage's own default and are stated
# because the frozen `lookup.json` and both score payloads were produced at
# that seed.
# score cells read wildtypes.json from their own --out; dispatch stages the
# frozen catalogue and, for the analyse cell, the frozen input set into each
# cell directory before the queue starts. Neither staged input is any cell's
# `expect` basename.
